instruments.source: Lucknow (MEDSKY PATH LAB & DIAGNOSTICS, business_unit_id 15) Mindray BS-series chemistry analyzer. Decoded from the site's eLab Assist logs, 26-30 Aug 2026 (logINMessage/logDetails): 1786 host queries, 2541 order records and 7067 results across 827 samples. The wire format matches the existing mindray ASTM dialect exactly (H field 12 RQ/PR/SA, barcode in the O Specimen ID field 4, analyte code in R component 1), so no protocol work was needed - only five analytes this site runs that the driver panel lacked.
_protocolNotes: ASTM E1381 framing + E1394 records, sender "Mindry", version 1394-97 - identical to the BS-430 the mindray dialect was originally decoded from. The host query arrives as H(RQ) + Q record with the barcode in Q field 3 ("^SID"); Synapse answers with the H(SA) + P + O download the dialect already builds. verify:mindray's 52 parity checks still pass unchanged.

TRANSPORT NOT OBSERVABLE from the eLab logs - they record framed messages, not the port. The BS-series speaks either RS-232 (9600 8-N-1, as at the reference site) or TCP. Serial is listed first because that is how the reference BS-430 runs; confirm on the analyzer's LIS screen at onboarding and switch the instrument if it is on Ethernet.

MODEL NOT IDENTIFIED BY THE WIRE: every BS-series analyzer signs its header "Mindry", so the logs cannot tell a BS-240 from a BS-360/430/480. The driverId here is a placeholder - pick the real model when adding the instrument. All BS models share this driver, so only the display name changes.
_mappingNotes: Every target was taken from what THIS site already registers in Noble, not carried over from another lab: 120 Lucknow samples were read back and each analyte matched to the test/parameter row it actually lands in. Same central Noble DB as the other presets, so the ids are directly comparable.

PRECISION: the analyzer transmits full internal precision (GLU 226.470520, CREAT 1.538779) where eLab writes a rounded figure - Noble holds 1.54, 7.55, 51.6, 109, 4. No change was needed: the mindray driver already rounds to 2 dp on parse (round2), a decision taken when the BS-430 was decoded, and verify:lucknow pins that it reproduces this site's stored values exactly.

ELECTROLYTES ARE NOT ON THIS ANALYZER. Na/K/Cl are registered against these samples in Noble but appear nowhere in the capture — zero results across 7067 R records AND zero orders across 1429 eLab order records, so the reference interface does not ask this analyzer for them either. They come from another instrument or an ISE module elsewhere. Mapping them here would make Synapse order tests eLab never orders on a bidirectional link; if this analyzer does gain an ISE module, add the codes it actually transmits rather than guessing Na/K/Cl.

SPOT-CHECK CAVEAT: comparing wire values against Noble across 80 analyte/sample pairs, most agree once per-analyte decimals are allowed for, but a few differ by a clean margin (SID 9366422 glucose wire 226.47 vs Noble 126.47; SID 8689560 uric acid 10.78 vs 8.78). Those SIDs show no re-run in the captured window, so they read as post-hoc amendments by the lab rather than an interfacing fault, and no conversion is applied. Worth confirming with the lab before go-live.

CODE SCAN CAVEAT (worth repeating for the next site): the transmitted-code list must be built by parsing every R record, not by regex over the raw text. A first pass here used an uppercase-only pattern and silently missed "Iron" — 588 results, the analyzer’s fifth-busiest channel. HDL, LDL, TIBC, UIBC, TC, TG, RFII and MAG are ordered by eLab but returned no result in the captured window; the first four are mapped ready, TC/TG are retired as duplicates, and RFII (rheumatoid factor, 70 orders) and MAG (magnesium, 1 order) are left unmapped pending a result to confirm their codes and targets.

mappings._note: Noble catalogues point glucose as three orderable variants - Fasting (BI114), Post Prandial (BI115) and Random (BI116) - while the analyzer has a single channel. Deliberately left at test level (no lisParamId) so Synapse's variant retargeting fills whichever variant the sample actually ordered; pinning a paramId would defeat it.

The analyzer measures UREA and Noble derives BUN (BI056) itself at /2.14 - verified here on SID 8689560: wire 51.60 -> Noble Urea 51.6, BUN 24.1. Write urea raw and never map this channel to the BUN field.
The analyzer runs the DSA method and reports direct bilirubin; Noble files it as the Conjugated parameter. Indirect (p432) is derived by Noble, not transmitted.
Albumin and Total Protein are parameters of the Noble composite BI213 at this site; Globulin and the A/G ratio are derived by Noble from the two, not transmitted.
Serum amylase. Noble also carries Amylase-Urine (BI032, t624) and Amylase - Body Fluid (BI028, t686); this analyzer runs serum, so those are intentionally not mapped.

Serum ADA. Noble also has ADA (Adenosine Deaminase) CSF (BI012, t18). Only 3 ADA results appear in the captured window, so confirm with the lab whether CSF ADA is ever run on this analyzer before relying on this target.

Mixed-case code on the wire ("Iron", not "IRON") — 588 results and 392 orders in the capture. The R record labels the unit "g/dL", which is the analyzer mislabelling micrograms; the magnitude is ug/dL and Noble stores ug/dL, so the value passes through unconverted. Do not add a g/dL conversion for it.
Ordered 697 times in the capture but returned no result in that window; the channel is real and the lab reports HDL, so it is mapped ready for when results arrive.
Ordered 697 times, no result in the captured window — same situation as HDL.
Ordered 547 times, no result in the captured window.
Ordered 540 times, no result in the captured window.

eLab orders BOTH CHOL and TC on every lipid panel, and both resolve to Noble Cholesterol - Total (BI079). Ordering two channels for one test is the duplicate-channel hazard that broke the Rohtak Getein, so only CHOL — the one that actually returns results (411 vs 0) — is mapped.
Same pairing as TC/CHOL: eLab orders both TRIG and TG, both resolve to Noble Triglycerides (BI218). Only TRIG returns results (403 vs 0), so TG is retired.

instruments.source: Lucknow (MEDSKY, business_unit_id 15) Agappe Mispa CX4 chemistry analyzer, added 2026-09-23 ahead of installation. Protocol from the Mispa CX4 user manual (REV.09-2017, §5.9 + Appendix E; the CX4 is a Dirui CS-400). Noble targets chosen from an aggregate read of this site's filled result rows over the last 180 days (which test/parameter row each analyte actually lands in, and its unit) — the same central catalog rows the Delhi CX4 preset targets, so the two presets carry an identical mapping list. NOT yet verified against a live unit: no serial capture existed when this was written.
_protocolNotes: RS-232 ONLY. The analyzer PC has no network host link; the manual lists COM 1-4 (never COM 1 per §5.9), default 19200 8-N-1 (4800/9600/19200 selectable). Reach it over LAN only through a serial-to-Ethernet device server, then pick tcp-server/tcp-client in Synapse.

On the analyzer: System Setup > Host Communication — tick Open Communication, tick Bidirectional, Data transmission mode = realtime, Gather sample mode = "Sample ID (Barcode)" (Sample No. mode carries no barcode and Synapse cannot file it), Sample save mode = First host, then Save and reboot the analyzer software (Appendix E step 4). "Simplified mode" and "Send QC Result To LIS" are undocumented on the wire — leave them off until a capture exists.

In Synapse tick Host Query so the Q record is answered. Each result record arrives in its own numbered frame; the barcode is component 1 of the O Specimen ID (SID^S.No^Disk^Pos^Dil). The order reply is one O record per test echoing that specimen id; a barcode with no Noble order is answered with a bare ENQ/EOT as the manual requires. verify:agappe-cx4 pins all of this to the manual's printed frames and checksums.

ITEM NAMES ARE SITE-CONFIGURABLE. The instrumentCode here is the factory item abbreviation from the manual's Appendix C (ALT, GGT, GLU(OX), Ca(CPC), …), which the analyzer sends as "^^^<abbr>". Whoever configures the chemistry parameters on this unit must either keep these abbreviations or rename the mapping rows to match — Synapse matches the code exactly (case-insensitive).

Ordering an item the analyzer does not have raises its "Illegal test item" alarm (code 143-49). Before go-live set every mapped row whose reagent is not loaded on this unit to ignored — particularly the ISE trio (K/Na/Cl) if no ISE module is fitted.

STOCK MENU ALTERNATES (from the Dirui interface protocol v1.1 Sample Register screen, which the CX4 software is built on): a unit set up from the stock item list sends TBIL/DBIL (not TB/DB), GLU (not GLU(OX)/GLU(HK)), CRE (single item), Ca (not Ca(CPC)/Ca(ARS)), P (not PHOS), Mb, APO A1, 5'-NT, U-HS-CRP, plus AFU, Cu, D-Dimer, ACE, GPDA, AFP, AMM, ACP, MAST and the L/H/I serum indices. The driver panel recognises all of these; if the Received panel shows them, rename the affected rows here (instrumentCode) rather than adding second live rows for the same Noble target.

The H-record sender/receiver are the "Analyzer ID" and "Host ID" typed on the Host Communication screen (the generic manual shows " Analyzer " / "Host"). Type CX4 as the Analyzer ID so Synapse's auto-discovery fingerprints the unit; the Host ID is free text. QC uploads ("Send QC Result To LIS": P name QC, O field 4 = control name^lot, Westgard flags) are recognised by the driver and dropped, so that option may stay on.
_mappingNotes: Volumes behind each target (180 days, this site): ALT 12.5k, AST 12k, uric acid 11.7k, creatinine 11.5k, bilirubin composite 11.3k, ALP 11k, Na/K 11k, GGT 10.7k, TP/ALB composite 10.7k, calcium 10.7k, chloride 10.3k, urea 10.2k, lipids 9.6k, iron/TIBC/UIBC 7.2-7.7k, glucose-fasting 6.6k, CRP 1.7k, phosphorus 1.6k, RF 1.5k, ferritin 0.5k, amylase 0.3k, lipase 0.3k, ADA 165, troponin I 75. Targets with no rows at this site are still listed (harmless: host query only sends what the sample ordered) so the two CX4 sites stay identical.

DUPLICATE-CHANNEL RULE: the CX4 menu carries two items for several analytes (GLU(HK)/GLU(OX), CRE/CRE-E, TB/TB-V, DB/DB-V, Ca(CPC)/Ca(ARS), PHOS/PHOS-S). Exactly one of each pair is mapped and the other is "ignored"; ordering both would run the test twice and race to fill one Noble cell. The mapped member is the Agappe standard kit — swap the pair if this unit is loaded with the other reagent.

UNITS: every mapped unit was read from Noble's stored rows at this site (testunit), not assumed. Where the CX4 factory unit disagrees with Noble the item is left unmapped (see _notMapped) rather than mapped with a silent conversion; convertForLis has no rules for these pairs.

OVERLAP: at Lucknow, the Mindray BS-series preset targets the same Noble rows for the core chemistry panel. Host query offers an ordered test to every instrument that maps it; decide per analyte which analyzer owns it and set the other to ignored.
_notMapped: HbA1C / HbA1c-S — HbA1c is owned by the Zeus D-20 HPLC (Delhi and Lucknow) and the Mispa Maestro; mapping the CX4 turbidimetric item would make host query offer HbA1c to two analyzers.
CK-MB — the CX4 item is an activity assay (U/L); Noble stores CK-MB as mass (BI259 ng/mL, CKMBFIA ng/mL). No conversion exists, so it stays unmapped.
APOA1 / APO B — Noble stores mg/dL (BI038/BI039); the CX4 factory item reports g/L. Map only after the analyzer item unit is set to mg/dL.
C3 / C4 — Noble mg/dL (BI082/MS023) vs CX4 g/L; same as Apo.
IgM — Noble mg/dL (BI256) vs CX4 g/L.
B2-MG — Noble ng/mL (BI042) vs CX4 mg/L (x1000).
Zn — Noble µg/dL (BI268) vs CX4 µmol/L.
LAC — Noble mg/dL (BI139) vs CX4 mmol/L.

ASO, PAMY, LAP, CHE, GLDH, ICDH, 5-NT, NAG, TPU, RBP, MYO, HBDH, A1-MG, PA, TRF, CO2 — no filled rows at either site in the last 180 days; left unmapped (Synapse still shows the result if the analyzer sends one).

mappings._note: Noble derives the SGOT/SGPT ratio (BI00012) itself; nothing to transmit.
Composite BI046 at both sites (59k rows Delhi / 11k Lucknow); the standalone "Bilirubin Total" BI048 (t89) is a minority row and is deliberately not targeted. Indirect (p432) is derived by Noble.

Duplicate channel of TB (vanadate-oxidation reagent). Two channels resolving to one Noble row is the duplicate-channel hazard that broke the Rohtak Getein; if the lab runs the vanadate kit instead of the diazo kit, swap: map TB-V to BI046/p431 and retire TB.
Duplicate channel of DB — see TB-V.
Composite BI213 (59k Delhi / 11k Lucknow). The standalone Total Protein BI186 (t153, ~3k) is not targeted; Globulin and A/G are derived by Noble.
Delhi files 575 rows in µmol/L; Lucknow none in the window (harmless — only ordered tests are sent).

Serum ADA. Noble also has ADA CSF (BI012, t18) and "FLUID FOR ADA" (BI360, t2089) — those are body-fluid orders; if the lab runs fluid ADA on this analyzer under the same item, the sample-level order decides which row is filled.

Test-level target on purpose (no lisParamId): Noble orders glucose as Fasting (BI114), Post Prandial (BI115) or Random (BI116) and Synapse's variant retargeting fills whichever the sample ordered. Agappe's standard glucose kit is GOD-PAP, hence the oxidase item is the live channel.
Duplicate channel of GLU(OX). If this site loads the hexokinase kit, swap: map GLU(HK) to BI114 (test level) and retire GLU(OX). Never leave both mapped — host query would order glucose twice.
Noble derives BUN (BI056) from urea at /2.14 and the BUN/Creatinine ratio itself. Write urea raw; never map a channel to the BUN row.

Retired: Noble derives BUN from the Urea row. If the lab only loads a BUN-calibrated kit, do NOT map it to BI056 — Noble's Urea row would stay empty; map UREA instead and calibrate the analyzer to report urea.
Serum creatinine (58k Delhi / 12k Lucknow). Noble's parameterised Creatinine rows (BI099 p507, BI195 p653, B2043 p399) are urine/ratio tests and are not targeted.
Duplicate channel of CRE. Swap if the site runs the enzymatic kit (map CRE-E to BI089, retire CRE).
Delhi only in the window (57 rows).

Urine microalbumin lands in parameter 401 of the ACR test (mg/L at both sites). The ratio (p400) is derived by Noble; urine creatinine (p399) would need a separate urine-creatinine item on the analyzer.
Delhi only (47 rows). Noble stores µmol/L, matching the analyzer.
Noble derives VLDL, non-HDL and every cholesterol ratio itself.
Delhi only (408 rows), mg/dL at both ends.
Delhi only (630 rows), µmol/L at both ends.
Delhi only (449 rows).
Serum LDH (Delhi 620 rows). "Lactate Dehydrogenase(any Fluid)" BI0360 is a body-fluid order and is not targeted.
Delhi 167 / Lucknow 75 rows, ng/mL. Only valid if the analyzer runs the Agappe turbidimetric hs-cTnI item; retire if troponin comes from an FIA reader.
Serum amylase; Amylase-Urine (BI032) and body-fluid amylase (BI028) are not targeted.

ONLY if the optional ISE module is fitted. Both sites file Na/K/Cl heavily (Delhi 56k, Lucknow 11k) but from another instrument today; an order for an item the analyzer lacks raises its "Illegal test item" alarm, so set K/Na/Cl to ignored at onboarding if there is no ISE.
See K.
See K. Noble labels the unit "mm0l/L" (typo in the catalog) — a label only.
Serum calcium. Ionized calcium (BI063) and 24h-urine calcium are separate orders.
Duplicate channel of Ca(CPC). Swap if the site runs the Arsenazo-III kit.
Delhi 693 rows; Lucknow none in the window.
Duplicate channel of PHOS (alternate reagent generation). Swap if that is the kit in use.
Noble stores µg/dL ("ug/dl") at both sites; the analyzer item must report µg/dL, not µmol/L.

The CX4 has no TIBC item (TIBC = Fe + UIBC). Noble's TIBC (BI138) and Transferrin Saturation (BI217) rows are filled heavily at both sites — confirm with the lab whether Noble derives them from Fe + UIBC or whether a TIBC item must be added on the analyzer.
Delhi only (683 rows). Separate Noble test from CRP, so both channels may stay mapped.

The only RF row either site files (Delhi 9k / Lucknow 1.5k), unit U/ml = IU/mL. Noble labels it "Nephelometry"; the CX4 assay is immunoturbidimetric — same scale, method label only. Confirm with the lab before go-live.
Turbidimetric ferritin. Ferritin is ALSO on the MAGICL/X3 immunoassay menus at Delhi — decide which analyzer owns it and set the other to ignored, or host query offers the order to both.
Delhi only (195 rows), g/L at both ends.
Delhi only (200 rows), g/L at both ends.
